summary.oneLiner: Alok Industries is one of India's largest vertically integrated textile companies with unique integration across both Cotton and Polyester segments, serving global retail brands, importers, and domestic manufacturers.
summary.business: Alok Industries operates a fully integrated textile manufacturing setup spanning spinning, weaving, processing, finished fabrics, home textiles, and garments in cotton, and continuous polymerization through to polyester yarns and staple fiber in polyester. The company serves a diversified customer base including global retail brands, textile importers, private labels, domestic retailers, garment exporters, and manufacturers across the world. Its operations are supported by large-scale, flexible plants in Vapi and Silvassa.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and availability (cotton)
risks.note: Cotton is the primary raw material; as an agricultural commodity, its prices are affected by weather, government policies, duties, and global supply-demand. This directly impacts cost of production and profitability.

risks.risk: Export market concentration and tariff exposure (USA)
risks.note: The USA reciprocal tariff regime escalated to 50% on Indian textile exports from August 2025, materially impacting export realizations. Policy uncertainty around the Bilateral Trade Agreement and relative tariff positioning versus competitors like Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Vietnam can rapidly redirect buyer sourcing decisions.

risks.risk: Demand slowdown and fashion trend shifts in value-added segments
risks.note: Performance depends on demand in individual business segments. Apparel Fabrics and Home Textiles are subject to fashion trends and consumer demand. Major international conflicts also impact demand from impacted economies and global markets.

risks.risk: Shipping route disruptions and elevated freight costs
risks.note: Ongoing disruptions to Red Sea shipping routes due to the Houthi conflict have continued to affect freight costs and transit times on key India-to-USA and India-to-Europe trade lanes, impacting export margin realizations and on-time delivery reliability.

risks.risk: Financial risk from high debt and interest rate sensitivity
risks.note: Outstanding term loans of â¹3,456.26 crores and working capital limits of â¹300 crores expose the company to interest obligations and repayment requirements. Loans are linked to MCLR, so any increase would raise interest costs.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Spinning:** Cotton and blended yarns in various counts
- **Polyester:** Polyester Chips, Partially Oriented Yarn (POY), Fully Drawn Yarn (FDY), Drawn Texturized Yarn (DTY), Polyester Staple Fiber (PSF)
- **Home Textiles:** Bedsheets, Towels

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global apparel brands accelerating supply chain diversification away from Bangladesh, a structural shift favoring large, integrated Indian manufacturers.
- Bangladesh graduating from LDC status on November 24, 2026, making India more competitive, reinforced by FTAs with UK and EU.
- Domestic apparel market projected to grow at ~9% CAGR to US$ 180 billion by 2030, driven by rising incomes, urbanization, GST rationalization, and evolving consumer preferences.
- Recovery in embroidery demand expected gradually as inflationary pressures ease in US/EU and consumer discretionary spending stabilises.
- Growth in home textiles driven by India's new FTAs with EU and UK, increasing demand for sustainable/certified products, and supply chain diversification by global brands.
- India's competitive strength in cotton-based woven fabrics supported by rising preference for natural fibers and shifting sourcing strategy.
- Increase demand in active wear and government PLI scheme on synthetic segment expected to strengthen India's global position.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Shift major polyester business to Manufacturing Capacity Booking (Job-work model) from March 2024.
- Elevate sustainability from compliance to core strategic priority, driving transformation across the value chain centred on circularity, renewable energy, and resource efficiency.
- Accelerate transition toward high-performance, sustainable fiber by leveraging Reliance Industries Limited's advanced Recron technologies (Kooltex, Green Gold) for a strategic shift toward technical home textiles and specialized blends.
- No explicit dividend policy, buyback, or reinvestment philosophy stated. The Board's Report confirms no buyback, no issue of shares with differential rights, no ESOP, and no change in capital structure during the year. CSR obligation is nil due to negative average net profit over the preceding three years.
- CSR Policy adopted in line with Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013; however, no CSR spend was required during the year as the average net profit of the three immediately preceding financial years was negative.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated operations across both cotton and polyester value chains, from spinning/polymerization to finished garments and home textiles.
- Diversified product, customer, and market mix spanning domestic, export, and converter-country channels, providing risk mitigation.
- Strong promoter background and group synergies with Reliance Industries Limited, supporting sustainability in challenging environments.
- Standalone credit rating of CARE AA+, reflecting strong business fundamentals.
